title: Rewrite aggregation digest and implement probabilistic TTL eviction to reduce stale console data
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: The console backend aggregation path has accumulated several small optimizations and one-off fixes over the last 18 months. This has resulted in brittle TTL semantics, duplicated rollup logic in two services, and Redis Lua scripts that can't be sharded safely. Symptoms we see: occasional stale dashboard numbers (1-5% of reads for high-throughput customers), tail latency spikes when large fanouts hit the aggregator, and memory churn due to ephemeral per-request caches.

Goal: Replace the current multi-service aggregation digest with a compact, shard-aware aggregator that enforces a probabilistic TTL eviction policy and a stale-read guard for critical metrics. The new implementation should reduce stale reads, lower 95/99th percentile latency for aggregation requests, and remove fragile Lua scripts so we can safely shard Redis clusters.

What this ticket covers (high-level):
- Introduce a single aggregation digest service (Go) that centralizes rollup semantics and emits deterministic cache keys.
- Implement probabilistic TTL eviction with backoff to reduce synchronized cache storms and stale reads.
- Add a read-path guard: on reads older than ttl_threshold, trigger a background refresh and return a best-effort fallback until fresh data is ready.
- Replace remaining Lua scripts with shard-aware pipelined mutations in the new service.
- Upgrade gqlgen (GraphQL server) and go-redis client to get support for new instrumentation hooks and better pipeline control.

Non-goals: Re-architecting the entire console data model or changing frontend contracts. This is a focused backend performance/consistency cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: New aggregation digest deployed behind a feature flag and serving a subset of console tenants
Stale-read rate for aggregated dashboard numbers reduced from ~2.8% to <0.5% for covered tenants
95th/99th percentile latency for aggregation requests reduced by at least 30% under representative load
No Lua scripts left in production aggregation path; Redis operations are shard-aware and pipelined
Observability: end-to-end tracing and dashboards added for aggregation hit/miss, eviction count, and refresh latency
tasks: Design compact aggregation digest schema and deterministic cache key format
Implement Go service: digest builder, TTL/eviction controller, background refresher
Replace Lua scripts with pipelined shard-aware mutations
Integrate with GraphQL resolver: switch hotpath to call new digest via gRPC and add timeouts/fallbacks
Upgrade dependencies: gqlgen -> v0.21.0, go-redis -> v9.0.0
Add tracing and metrics (OpenTelemetry): cache hits, evictions, refresh latency
Rollout behind flag: canary on low-traffic orgs, monitor, then ramp
Write integration tests that simulate concurrent writes and verify no stale regressions
